verses.text: Jephthah from Gilead was a strong warrior, but he was born to a sex worker. His father was Gilead. 🛡️
Gilead’s wife had sons too. When they grew up, they pushed Jephthah out: ‘You’re not getting any inheritance from our dad. You’re another woman’s son.’ 😠
Jephthah ran from his brothers and settled in Tob. A crew of outlaws gathered around him and went out with him. 🏃
Some time later, Ammon’s people went to war against Israel. ⚔️
When Ammon attacked Israel, Gilead’s elders went to Tob to bring Jephthah back. 📣
They told Jephthah, ‘Come be our commander, so we can fight Ammon.’ 🗣️
Jephthah said, ‘Didn’t you hate me and kick me out of my father’s home? Why come looking for me now that you’re in trouble?’ 😤
Gilead’s elders answered, ‘That’s why we’ve come back—we want you to fight Ammon with us. You’ll lead everyone in Gilead.’ 🤝
Jephthah said, ‘If you bring me back to fight Ammon, and Yahweh hands them over to me, will I really lead you?’ ⚖️
The elders said, ‘Yahweh will hear this agreement between us. We’ll do what you say.’ 🤝
Jephthah went with them, and the people made him their commander and leader. He repeated all his words before Yahweh at Mizpah. 🙏
Jephthah sent messengers to Ammon’s king: ‘What’s your issue with me? Why come fight my land?’ 📨
Ammon’s king replied, ‘Because Israel took my land when they came up from Egypt—from the Arnon to the Jabbok and the Jordan. So give that territory back peacefully.’ 🗺️
Jephthah sent messengers back to Ammon’s king with another reply. 📨
He said, ‘Jephthah says: Israel didn’t take Moab’s land or Ammon’s land. 📜
‘When Israel came up from Egypt, they traveled through the wilderness to the Red Sea and reached Kadesh. 🏜️
‘Israel sent messengers to Edom’s king: “Please let us pass through your land,” but he said no. They asked Moab’s king too, and he also refused. So Israel stayed at Kadesh. 🚫
‘Then Israel traveled through the wilderness, went around Edom and Moab, and came along Moab’s eastern side. They camped beyond the Arnon, without crossing Moab’s border—the Arnon was the border. 🗺️
‘Israel sent messengers to Sihon, king of the Amorites who ruled from Heshbon: “Please let us pass through your land to our destination.” 📨
‘Sihon didn’t trust Israel to cross his border. He gathered his people, camped at Jahaz, and fought Israel. ⚔️
‘But Yahweh, Israel’s God, handed Sihon and all his people over to Israel. Israel defeated them and took the Amorites’ whole land. 🛡️
‘Israel took all the Amorite territory, from the Arnon to the Jabbok, and from the wilderness to the Jordan. 🗺️
‘So now Yahweh, Israel’s God, has driven the Amorites out ahead of his people. Why should you take their land? ⚖️
‘Don’t you take whatever Chemosh your god gives you? In the same way, we’ll take whatever Yahweh our God has driven out before us. 🙏
‘Are you really greater than Balak son of Zippor, Moab’s king? Did he ever challenge Israel or fight us? 👑
‘For three hundred years Israel lived in Heshbon and its towns, Aroer and its towns, and all the towns along the Arnon. Why didn’t you reclaim them during all that time? ⏳
‘I haven’t sinned against you, but you’re wrong to make war on me. Let Yahweh, the Judge, decide today between Israel and Ammon.’ ⚖️
But Ammon’s king ignored Jephthah’s message. 📭
Then Yahweh’s Spirit came on Jephthah. He traveled through Gilead and Manasseh, through Mizpah in Gilead, and onward toward Ammon. 🕊️
Jephthah made a vow to Yahweh: ‘If you hand Ammon over to me, 🙏
‘then whatever comes out of my house to meet me when I return safely from Ammon will belong to Yahweh, and I’ll offer it up as a burnt offering.’ 🔥
Jephthah crossed over to fight Ammon, and Yahweh handed them over to him. ⚔️
He struck them from Aroer all the way to Minnith—twenty towns—and as far as Abel-Keramim. Ammon was crushed before Israel. 🛡️
Jephthah came home to Mizpah, and his daughter came out to meet him with tambourines and dancing. She was his only child; he had no other son or daughter. 🥁
When he saw her, he tore his clothes and cried, ‘Oh, my daughter! You’ve brought me down and filled my heart with grief. I made a vow to Yahweh, and I can’t take it back.’ 💔
She said, ‘Dad, you made that vow to Yahweh. Do to me what you promised, since Yahweh has given you victory over your enemies, Ammon.’ 😢
Then she asked her father, ‘Please do this one thing for me: give me two months to go into the mountains with my friends and mourn that I’ll die without marrying.’ 🏔️
He said, ‘Go.’ He let her leave for two months. She and her friends went into the mountains and mourned that she would never marry. 😢
After two months she returned to her father, and he carried out the vow he had made. She had never been with a man. This became a custom in Israel. 🕊️
Every year Israel’s young women would go out for four days to remember Jephthah’s daughter from Gilead. 🌿
